Waste management impacts were not considered at this stage of the study; however, waste flows are documented in the life cycle inventory for reference and available in Appendix B: Detailed Life Cycle Inventory Data. 2.9.4 Life Cycle Impact Assessment The LCA model was developed in openLCA v2.5.0. Global warming potential (GWP) is the only life cycle impact assessment category considered in this study. Characterization factors are sourced from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Sixth Assessment Report (AR6) using a 100-year time horizon (IPCC, 2021). Results using characterization factors from previous IPCC assessment reports are included in Appendix A: Detailed Life Cycle Results. An uncertainty analysis was performed on natural gas, electricity, and CO storage parameters to 2 determine high- and low-end impacts for each pathway and scenario. The uncertainty analysis for each parameter is discussed further in Section 2.10.5. 2.9.5 Types and Sources of Data Inventory data has been collected from various government sources, commercial references, and academic publications. This section describes data sources related to all modeled upstream and downstream processes in the inventory: • All process mass and energy flow data in the ammonia plant were modeled according to the Aspen cost and performance model for this baseline. In each modeling case, mass and energy flows crossing the facility/plant boundary to enter the environment or technosphere were tallied in a stream table for inclusion in the inventory. Flow amounts were normalized to 1 kg of ammonia production. Overall and component mass balances were validated for the life cycle inventory. Inputs crossing the facility boundary include air, electricity, natural gas, and water. Outputs crossing the facility boundary include argon, CO (co-product), CO (emission), hydrogen, nitrogen, oxygen, methyl mercaptan, 2 2 and water. All mass and energy flows in the facility black box model are included in this analysis and are subject to the assumptions presented in previous sections. Complete inventories of flows included for each case in the openLCA database are included in Appendix B: Detailed Life Cycle Inventory Data. • Upstream electricity generation was modeled using the EPA and NETL/EPA Electricity Life Cycle Inventory (eLCI) (2022), with a data vintage of 2022. The emissions profile for the U.S. average scenario is provided by the eLCI U.S. average consumption mix, at user, and the emissions profile for the Midwest scenario is provided by the eLCI Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) balancing authority consumption mix, at user. For both location scenarios, the low-end and high-end sensitivity values correspond to the 5th and 95th percentile results, respectively, from a Monte Carlo simulation with 1,000 iterations, where emissions in the underlying generation technologies include lognormal uncertainty to account for differences between facilities within a balancing authority. 27 COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL, STATE-OF-THE-ART, FOSSIL-BASED AMMONIA PRODUCTION • Upstream production of natural gas was modeled using the NETL natural gas model, with a data vintage of 2020,
